page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance tradeoff. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by lower scores in single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench tests. However, the instance achieves average multi-core performance in Geekbench and Passmark CPU tests, leveraging its 24 threads. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average tier, with uncached read speeds of 96.89 GB/sec and write speeds of 52.55 GB/sec.

Given its high memory density and average multi-core processing capabilities, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-thread performance. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, and multi-threaded data processing tasks. The lack of local storage requires attaching external block storage for persistent data.

Built on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance provides a high memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct tradeoff: single-core processing is weak, but multi-core execution and memory bandwidth fall into the average tier. The instance delivers 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Qualitatively, the ecs.se1ne.6xlarge offers a cost-effective profile for memory-heavy workloads that benefit from parallel execution rather than raw single-threaded speed. It is highly suitable for database hosting, in-memory caching, and general-purpose multi-threaded enterprise applications.
